# Results summary (generated by experiments/summarize.py from the raw files in this folder)

All data is **synthetic** and every workload is **generated or simulated**. Intervals are 95% percentile bootstrap intervals over seeds unless stated. Nothing here describes a real business.

## E3: calculators against independent references (24 Monte Carlo cases x 200,000 draws)

### The product against every check

| Check | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| c01_ppf_published_constants | pass | max abs error 7.99e-15 |
| c02_ppf_round_trip | pass | max |cdf(ppf(p)) - p| = 2.22e-16 |
| c03_lead_time_sd_vs_monte_carlo | pass | worst relative error 0.0050 over 24 cases |
| c04a_cycle_service_vs_monte_carlo_fixed_lead_time | pass | 0 of 36 (case, level) pairs outside 4 standard errors; worst deviation 0.44x tolerance |
| c04b_cycle_service_vs_monte_carlo_random_lead_time | pass | 0 of 36 outside 0.01; worst |achieved - target| = 0.0056 |
| c05_fill_rate_formula_vs_monte_carlo | pass | 0 of 72 outside tolerance; worst deviation 0.29x tolerance |
| c06_fill_rate_sizing_vs_monte_carlo | pass | 0 of 72 outside tolerance; worst deviation 0.33x tolerance |
| c07_eoq_vs_brute_force_search | pass | 0 of 30 random cases more than 1 unit from the brute-force optimum |
| c08a_rounding_is_feasible | pass | 0 of 60 results not a multiple of the pack size or below the minimum |
| c08b_cost_rounding_is_cheapest_feasible | pass | 0 of 60 results dearer than the cheapest feasible quantity |
| c08c_up_rounding_is_smallest_feasible_at_or_above | pass | 0 of 60 results differ from the smallest feasible quantity at or above the request |
| c09_exact_poisson_where_normal_is_adequate | pass | worst |exact service level - target| = 0.0234 for lambda*L >= 50 (limit 0.03) |
| c10_ses_vs_closed_form | pass | max abs difference 3.55e-15 |
| c11_croston_vs_definition | pass | max abs difference 2.22e-15 |
| c12_reorder_point_composition | pass | max relative difference 1.05e-15 |
| c13_abc_vs_independent_implementation | pass | 0 of 20 random value sets classified differently |
| c14_safety_stock_monotonicity | pass | service level, lead time, lead-time variability and demand variability each raise the requirement |

### Deliberately broken variants: 17 of 17 caught

| Broken variant | What is wrong | Caught | By |
|---|---|---|---|
| ss_ignores_lead_time_variance | lead-time variability left out: sigma_LT = sd*sqrt(L) | yes | c03_lead_time_sd_vs_monte_carlo; c04b_cycle_service_vs_monte_carlo_random_lead_time; c14_safety_stock_monotonicity |
| ss_sigma_times_L | demand variability scaled by L instead of sqrt(L) | yes | c03_lead_time_sd_vs_monte_carlo; c04a_cycle_service_vs_monte_carlo_fixed_lead_time; c04b_cycle_service_vs_monte_carlo_random_lead_time; c09_exact_poisson_where_normal_is_adequate |
| ss_adds_instead_of_quadrature | the two variability terms are added instead of combined in quadrature | yes | c03_lead_time_sd_vs_monte_carlo; c04b_cycle_service_vs_monte_carlo_random_lead_time |
| ss_wrong_tail | z taken from 1 - service level | yes | c04a_cycle_service_vs_monte_carlo_fixed_lead_time; c04b_cycle_service_vs_monte_carlo_random_lead_time; c09_exact_poisson_where_normal_is_adequate; c14_safety_stock_monotonicity |
| ss_z_rounded_to_one_decimal | z rounded to one decimal place | yes | c04a_cycle_service_vs_monte_carlo_fixed_lead_time; c04b_cycle_service_vs_monte_carlo_random_lead_time |
| ppf_logistic_approximation | inverse normal replaced by a crude logistic approximation | yes | c01_ppf_published_constants; c02_ppf_round_trip; c04a_cycle_service_vs_monte_carlo_fixed_lead_time |
| eoq_missing_factor_2 | EOQ = sqrt(D*K/h) (factor 2 missing) | yes | c07_eoq_vs_brute_force_search |
| eoq_monthly_demand | EOQ computed from monthly instead of yearly demand | yes | c07_eoq_vs_brute_force_search |
| round_down_to_pack | quantities rounded down to the pack size | yes | c08b_cost_rounding_is_cheapest_feasible; c08c_up_rounding_is_smallest_feasible_at_or_above |
| moq_ignored | minimum order quantity ignored | yes | c08b_cost_rounding_is_cheapest_feasible |
| fill_rate_not_scaled_by_Q | fill rate = 1 - G(z) (sigma/Q scaling missing) | yes | c05_fill_rate_formula_vs_monte_carlo |
| loss_function_wrong_sign | normal loss function with the wrong sign | yes | c05_fill_rate_formula_vs_monte_carlo |
| ses_alpha_swapped | smoothing constant and its complement swapped | yes | c10_ses_vs_closed_form |
| croston_counts_zeros_not_intervals | Croston interval counts the zeros between demands instead of the interval | yes | c11_croston_vs_definition |
| rop_forgets_safety_stock | reorder point = lead-time demand only | yes | c12_reorder_point_composition |
| rop_lead_time_in_weeks | lead time converted to weeks but demand kept per day | yes | c12_reorder_point_composition |
| abc_inclusive_share | ABC thresholds applied to the cumulative share including the item | yes | c13_abc_vs_independent_implementation |

### Exact Poisson enumeration: service level actually delivered by the normal-model reorder point (informational)

| Expected demand over the lead time (lambda x L) | Result |
|---|---|
| below 10 | 30 cells; exact service minus target: mean +0.026, range -0.001 to +0.081 |
| 10 to 50 | 18 cells; exact service minus target: mean +0.013, range +0.000 to +0.035 |
| 50 and above | 12 cells; exact service minus target: mean +0.008, range +0.000 to +0.023 |

A positive gap means the exact service level is above the target (the normal model is conservative); a negative gap means it falls short.
